GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
Before sending any privileged information to or interacting with an external party on behalf of the user, the assistant should assess the recipient's trustworthiness and whether the disclosure is reasonable and within the scope of the user's request.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - root_authority: Rules in the protect_privileged_information section carry root authority.
  - scope_of_autonomy: The scope of the user's request, referenced by the privileged information rule.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1707_1973_n027' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):

Before sending any privileged information to or interacting with an external party on behalf of the user, the assistant should assess the recipient’s trustworthiness and whether the disclosure is reasonable and within the [scope](#scope_of_autonomy) of the user’s request.

CROSS-REFERENCED CLAUSES — the text of every clause this one points at.
Use these to know what the names mean. Do NOT translate them here.
